adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed get "users" admin route with no deprecation or alias, causing existing clients calling /admin/groups/:id/users to 404

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `get "users"` route under `admin/groups` and replaces it with `put "members"` and `delete "members"`. However, the finding’s claim that this “causes existing clients calling /admin/groups/:id/users to 404” is not verifiable from the diff: the updated JS code no longer calls `/admin/groups/:id/users` (it uses `/admin/groups/:id/members.json`), and nothing in the diff shows any remaining internal callers depending on the old endpoint. So the only provable fact is an API change, not an introduced bug within this change set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: members endpoint no longer bounds limit parameter, so ?limit=1000000 can serialize the entire membership of a huge group in one request

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then runs `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serializes `members`. There is no upper bound enforced on `limit`, so a request like `?limit=1000000` will attempt to load and serialize up to that many users (or the whole group if it has fewer), which is a concrete performance/DoS risk. The diff does not introduce any cap to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 user lookups in add_members: usernames.split(",").each { User.find_by_username(username) } runs one query per username instead of a single User.where(username_lower: names)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff introduces `usernames.split(",").each do |username|; if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end; end`, which performs one database lookup per username. With many usernames this results in multiple queries where a single `WHERE username_lower IN (...)` (or similar) query would suffice. This is a concrete performance issue visible in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members calls group.save per member and does individual inserts instead of a bulk insert

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates over usernames and calls `group.add(user)` for each user, but it only calls `group.save` once after the loop (`if group.save ...`). So the claim that it "calls group.save per member" is not supported by the diff. The remaining point about "individual inserts instead of a bulk insert" is at best an optimization speculation: the diff does not show what `group.add` does internally, and there is no clear correctness/security defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember triggers a full findMembers() refetch after every single removal, with no error handling so a failed DELETE leaves stale UI

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#removeMember` does issue a DELETE and, on success (`.then`), calls `self.findMembers()` to refresh the members list. That refetch is intentional and is bounded by `limit/offset` (not necessarily a “full” refetch of all members). Also, there is no optimistic UI removal shown in the diff, so if the DELETE fails the UI will typically remain unchanged (still showing the member), which matches server state rather than becoming “stale”. While there is no explicit error handling/message for a failed DELETE or a failed subsequent refetch, the specific claim that it “leaves stale UI” is not directly verifiable from the diff as a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination off-by-one: 'next' clamps offset to user_count and totalPages uses floor(count/limit)+1, producing partially filled or empty last page (e.g., count=100, limit=50 gives 3 pages with empty page 3), causing a wasted request and UI confusion

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces pagination calculations that are off by one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, so `user_count=100, limit=50` yields 3 pages instead of 2. The `next` action clamps `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, so from offset 50 it can become 100. Then `currentPage` becomes `Math.floor(100/50)+1 = 3`, and `findMembers` allows `offset == user_count`, making an AJAX request that will return an empty `members` list. This matches the proposed finding (wasted request/empty last page).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded usernames payload accepted server-side in add_members with no cap on number of usernames, making the N+1 worst-case unbounded

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the server accepts a required `usernames` parameter and iterates `usernames.split(",")` with `User.find_by_username(username)` and `group.add(user)` inside the loop. There is no validation or cap on how many usernames can be submitted, so a single request can trigger an unbounded number of per-username DB lookups and membership operations (classic N+1 behavior) proportional to the payload size. This is directly visible in the diff and is a real performance/DoS risk even if the endpoint is admin-scoped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PUT /admin/groups/:id silently drops nested group[usernames] payload, returning 200 while memberships remain unchanged

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, Admin::GroupsController#update was rewritten to read top-level params (:alias_level, :visible, :name) and it no longer processes params[:group] or any :usernames field at all. Membership changes were intentionally moved to new endpoints (PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members via add_members and DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members via remove_member), and the updated JS model (Group#save / #create) no longer sends nested group[...] or usernames. So while a legacy client sending group[usernames] would indeed be ignored and could still get a 200, that behavior matches an intentional API change shown in the diff rather than an introduced defect in the updated code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH /admin/groups/:id incremental add/delete membership semantics removed with no replacement route

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the old incremental membership update via PATCH /admin/groups/:id (the `update_patch` method and `changes: {add/delete}` handling are gone, and `update` now only updates alias_level/visible/name). However, there *is* a replacement route added in `config/routes.rb`: `PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` -> `add_members` and `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` -> `remove_member`, with corresponding controller actions implemented. So the claim "removed with no replacement route" is not verifiable from the diff (replacement endpoints exist), even though the exact PATCH semantics are removed/changed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: POST /admin/groups request payload shape changed from nested group[...] to flat params, breaking existing clients and possibly creating groups with empty names

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#create from reading nested params (previously `params[:group][:name]`, `params[:group][:visible]`, etc.) to reading flat params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`). The JS model was updated accordingly (`Discourse.ajax("/admin/groups", { data: this.asJSON() })` now sends flat keys), but any existing client still POSTing the old `group[...]` payload will now result in `params[:name]` being nil and the controller setting `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip` (blank). Whether that creates an “empty name” group depends on model validations, but the request shape/API contract change is directly verifiable in the diff and would break old clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET /groups/:group_id/members response shape changed from array to wrapped {members: [], meta: {}} object with no compatibility layer

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (an array JSON response) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, i.e., a wrapped object response. There is no code in the controller providing an alternate/legacy array format, so any existing client calling `GET /groups/:group_id/members` and expecting an array will break unless updated (only some internal JS callers were updated to use `result.members`/`result.meta`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Default 200-member page size for automatic groups removed; every group now defaults to limit=50, silently truncating membership lists

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, whereas previously only *automatic* groups were limited/offset (defaulting to 200) and non-automatic groups returned the full ordered member list. On the client, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now requests `limit`/`offset` and defaults `limit` to 50, so only the first 50 members are fetched by default. The public `group/members.hbs` template was changed to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, but no pagination UI is added there in this diff, so users beyond the first page won’t be shown unless some other (not-shown) navigation exists. This is a verifiable behavior change that can truncate displayed membership lists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET /admin/groups/users route removed with no replacement or deprecation, causing 404 for external tooling

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `GET /admin/groups/users` route (`get "users"` is deleted in `config/routes.rb`), but the proposed impact (“causing 404 for external tooling”) is not verifiable from the diff and is speculative. The UI/model changes shown also stop relying on that route and instead use `/groups/:name/members.json` for listing members and `PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json` for membership changes, so there *is* functional replacement for the apparent purpose. There’s no evidence in the diff that anything in-repo still calls `/admin/groups/users` or that its removal is an unintended bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members endpoint silently skips nonexistent usernames and returns success even when no users were added

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. Nonexistent usernames are simply ignored. The method does not track whether any users were actually added, and it returns `success_json` whenever `group.save` succeeds. Since `group.save` will typically succeed even if nothing changed, the endpoint can return success even when all provided usernames were nonexistent (i.e., zero members added).

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete on a has_many :through association followed by group.save, which may not persist membership removal

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In Rails, calling `delete` on a `has_many`/`has_many :through` (or HABTM) association issues SQL to remove the join row(s) immediately; it does not require `group.save` to persist the membership removal. The subsequent `group.save` is redundant but does not prevent or undo the deletion. Therefore the finding that the removal "may not persist" is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member returns success even when user_id doesn't correspond to a member (silent no-op)

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. If `user_id` is not currently a member, `delete` is effectively a no-op and `group.save` will still typically succeed, so the endpoint will return success. However, nothing in the diff establishes that this should be treated as an error (and prior specs in this area historically allowed “remove non-members” to succeed silently). So while the observation is accurate about behavior, it’s not a clearly verifiable defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member client sends user_id as DELETE body param, which may not be parsed reliably, causing params.require(:user_id) to 400

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the client issues `Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + id + '/members.json', { type: 'DELETE', data: { user_id: ... } })`, and the Rails controller action `remove_member` does `params.require(:user_id)`. Rails/ActionDispatch does parse request parameters for DELETE requests (including form-encoded bodies), and Discourse.ajax is a jQuery-style request that will send `data` as standard parameters. Nothing in the diff shows a mismatch in content type, routing, or parameter names that would cause `user_id` to be missing consistently. The claim that DELETE bodies “may not be parsed reliably” is environment/speculation rather than a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Frontend group members template iterates `members` which is never set on the members controller, rendering an empty list

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` the loop changed from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`. But in `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, `setupController` now does `controller.set("model", model);` (where `model` is the Group from `modelFor('group')`) and only calls `model.findMembers()` without ever setting `controller.members`. Previously, the route populated `_members` and set `controller.model` to that array, so the template rendered. With this diff, unless the group-members controller is an ObjectController proxying `members` from `model` (not shown in the diff), `members` will be undefined and the list will render empty.

adjudication_records.issue_text: asJSON() dropped the {group: ...} wrapper without a shim, changing the client-side model's serialized payload shape for external plugins

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` from `{ group: {...} }` to a flat object, but the only visible callers in this diff (`create()` and `save()`) were also updated to send `data: this.asJSON()` and the Rails controller endpoints were changed to read top-level params (`params[:name]`, `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`) instead of `params[:group]`. So within the shown codebase, the payload shape change is consistent and not a demonstrable defect. The claim about “external plugins” breaking is not verifiable from this diff and is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group creation UI no longer supports adding members in one step, requiring two round trips and risking memberless groups on mid-failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the ability to create a group while simultaneously adding members. Previously, the controller’s save action called `group.createWithUsernames(this.get('usernames'))` / `saveWithUsernames(...)`, and the model sent `usernames` in `asJSON` under `group`. After the change, `save` calls `group.save()` and `create` calls `group.create()`, and `Discourse.Group#asJSON` no longer includes `usernames`. The admin template also only renders the add-members UI inside `{{#if id}} ... {{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}} {{/if}}`, meaning the user selector/button won’t appear until after the group has been created (has an id). Therefore adding members requires a second request (`addMembers` -> PUT /admin/groups/:id/members.json), making creation+membership non-atomic and allowing a successfully-created but memberless group if the second step fails.

For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that using Math.floor(user_count/limit) + 1 causes an extra/phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit and suggests Math.ceil, which is the same pagination bug described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: next action clamps offset to user_count allowing navigation to an empty page rendering zero members
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same issue: in the next action, clamping the offset to user_count can make offset == total, resulting in an empty final page (0 members) and confusing UX.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No error handling in findMembers, removeMember, and addMembers AJAX calls — failures leave member list stale with no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Group.findMembers`, `removeMember`, and `addMembers` methods that call `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` but never attach any error handling (`catch`/failure callbacks). Additionally, the controller actions often don’t consume/return these promises in a way that would surface failures (e.g., `removeMember` action triggers `model.removeMember(member)` inside `bootbox.confirm` without handling its rejection; `setupController` calls `model.findMembers()` without chaining). If the AJAX request fails, the success-path `setProperties`/`findMembers()` refresh won’t run, and there’s no local user-facing feedback or retry behavior in this code. Any feedback would have to come from some global `Discourse.ajax` error handler not shown in the diff, so the finding (as stated) is a verifiable issue in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupController fire-and-forgets model.findMembers() in admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6, swallowing failures entirely

adjudication.rationale: In both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6`, `setupController` calls `model.findMembers();` without returning/awaiting the promise or attaching error handling. Previously, the routes used `afterModel` and returned `model.findMembers().then(...)`, meaning the transition would wait for the request and a rejection would propagate through the route’s promise chain. After this change, failures from `Discourse.ajax(...)` inside `findMembers` are no longer tied to the route lifecycle, so request errors can be effectively ignored from the route’s perspective (page renders without members and without a route-level failure). This is a real behavioral/correctness regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: automatic in group_member.hbs resolves against the member (Discourse.User) instead of the group, so the remove-link guard never works for automatic groups
Spec uses xhr :put for remove_member but the route is delete, so the automatic-group removal protection is untested

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin groups membership removal endpoint is declared as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, and the JS model calls it with `type: "DELETE"`. However, in spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb the new `.remove_member` context uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, which does not match the routed verb and could let the test pass while not reflecting the real DELETE-only endpoint. This makes the spec not accurately testing the routed behavior for automatic-group removal protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members endpoint has no upper cap on limit parameter, allowing unbounded serialization of large group memberships (DoS vector)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code takes `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and then serializes the result into JSON. There is no upper bound enforced on `limit`, so a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` value and force the server to fetch and serialize a very large member list. This is a verifiable unbounded query/serialization risk in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative or huge offsets are also unvalidated on the members endpoint

adjudication.rationale:
In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes pagination to always use `limit` and `offset` from request params:

```rb
limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i
offset = params[:offset].to_i
members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)
```

There is no validation/clamping of `offset` (or `limit`) on the server side. A client can supply a negative offset (e.g. `offset=-10`), which Rails will pass to the DB via `OFFSET -10` (behavior varies by DB/adapter, but can error or behave unexpectedly). A very large offset is also accepted and can cause inefficient queries. Although the new JS client code clamps offsets, the endpoint itself remains unvalidated and is callable directly, so the finding is a real, diff-verifiable issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips non-existent usernames with no error in response, giving admin false success feedback

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; otherwise it does nothing. There is no tracking of missing usernames and the response is still `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it typically will even if nothing was added). So a request containing non-existent usernames can return success while adding nobody, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route setupController does not return the findMembers promise, regressing from previous afterModel pattern that paused router on failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `afterModel` hooks in both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6` that previously did `return model.findMembers().then(...)`, which would keep the transition waiting and route errors would propagate via the normal promise rejection path. It replaces this with `setupController(...){ controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers(); }` without returning/awaiting the promise. In Ember, `setupController` is not a promise-aware hook, so the router will not pause for `findMembers`, and failures/rejections won’t be handled the same way as when returned from `afterModel`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for changed public API of GroupsController#members: response format with members/meta and pagination contract untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (an array response) to a new JSON shape `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and introduces pagination params (`limit` default 50, `offset`). In the provided spec changes, only `Admin::GroupsController` is tested; there is no test added/updated for the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint to assert the new `members/meta` response contract or pagination behavior. So the changed API is untested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for pagination edge cases in members endpoint (offset beyond total, limit=0, default params) or guardian.ensure_can_see! blocking non-visible groups

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce pagination parameters (limit/offset) in GroupsController#members and does not add any corresponding specs for those edge cases or for guardian.ensure_can_see! behavior. However, the proposed finding is about missing test coverage rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect in the changed code itself. Nothing in the diff indicates pagination or guardian checks are broken—only that they aren't explicitly tested here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed incremental-membership edge-case tests (non-existent user add, removing non-member, removing non-existent user) not ported to add_members/remove_member

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the prior “incremental” membership tests (adding non-existent users, removing non-members, etc.) and does not clearly replace them with equivalent coverage for the new add_members/remove_member endpoints. However, this is a test coverage reduction rather than a verifiable runtime bug/correctness defect introduced by the code change. The new controller methods also appear to handle these cases benignly (non-existent usernames are ignored; deleting a non-member user_id is effectively a no-op), so the finding doesn’t point to an actual functional problem in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages off-by-one: floor(user_count/limit)+1 reports an extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, so showingLast is never true and next navigates to an empty page

adjudication.rationale: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (except when user_count == 0). When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users with limit 50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2. The `next` action allows `offset` to become `user_count` (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), and `findMembers` will then request `offset=100`, which the server will return as an empty `members` list (since it does `.limit(limit).offset(offset)`). This creates an extra, empty last page (page 3) and enables navigation to it due to the off-by-one `totalPages` calculation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unit tests for frontend pagination computed properties (totalPages, currentPage, offset clamping in findMembers)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new frontend pagination logic (currentPage/totalPages computed properties and offset clamping in Group#findMembers), but the diff does not include any frontend/unit test framework changes or an established requirement that such computed properties must be unit-tested. The absence of JS unit tests in this diff is not a verifiable bug/correctness defect introduced by the change; it’s a process/coverage suggestion rather than a concrete problem demonstrable from the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update test hardcodes automatic group id 1 based on implicit fixture assumption and only asserts the negative case; no positive test that updating a non-automatic group persists name, alias_level, visible

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` the new update spec does `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, ...` and then `Group.find(1)` without fabricating/creating that group inside the example. That hard-codes an ID and relies on an implicit preexisting automatic group with id=1 in the test database/fixtures, which is a brittle assumption introduced by this diff. The second part about missing a positive update test is more about coverage than a concrete defect, but the hardcoded ID issue is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update action contract change (flat params instead of nested :group) is untested since old tests were deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change Admin::GroupsController#update from nested params[:group] to flat params (e.g., params[:name], params[:visible], params[:alias_level]). However, this contract change is explicitly covered by a new spec in the ".update" context: `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, name: "WAT", visible: "true"`, which exercises the new flat-params behavior (and verifies name change is ignored for automatic groups while visible is updated). While older update/member-related tests were removed, membership updates were moved to new endpoints (add_members/remove_member), so the deletion doesn’t make the update contract untested. Therefore the finding is not a verifiable problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create no longer accepts usernames but no test asserts the old nested payload is rejected or ignored, and the new error path (render_json_error on invalid/duplicate name) is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Admin::GroupsController#create` to accept top-level `params[:name]` and drop `usernames` on create (membership now handled via new `add_members`). However, the proposed finding is about *missing tests* (not asserting the old nested payload is rejected/ignored, and not testing `render_json_error` on invalid/duplicate names). That is a test-coverage concern rather than a verifiable functional bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff. The updated JS client also switches to sending the new payload shape, so there’s no demonstrated in-repo breakage in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers empty-name path returns undefined instead of a promise, breaking any future caller that chains .then
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: a function has an execution path with no explicit return, causing it to return undefined. The candidate frames it specifically as the empty-name path returning undefined (instead of the expected promise), which is a concrete instance of the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members does not strip whitespace when splitting usernames, so 'user1, user2' silently fails to find user2, and there is no test covering this

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)`. It never `strip`s each token, so an input like "user1, user2" yields " user2" (leading space) and `find_by_username` will not match the real username, causing that member not to be added with no error. The added spec for adding several members uses `join(",")` (no spaces), so this whitespace case is not covered by tests in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test uses xhr :put for remove_member but route is delete, causing spec to fail or pass for wrong reason
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue highlights the same mismatch: the test calls remove_member with xhr :put while the route is defined as a DELETE route, which can cause incorrect behavior in the spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages calculation: exact multiples of limit produce wrong page count, so showingLast never true and next fetches empty offset

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). For exact multiples of `limit` this overcounts by 1. Example: `user_count=100`, `limit=50` => `floor(2)+1=3` pages, but only 2 pages exist. `next` computes `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, so from page 2 (`offset=50`) it advances to `offset=100`. `Group.findMembers` then requests `/members.json` with `offset=100`, and the server applies `limit(...).offset(100)` which yields an empty result set. Only then does `currentPage` become 3 and `showingLast` become true. This matches the finding: wrong page count prevents `showingLast` from being true on the real last page and allows fetching an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated pagination/offset clamping logic in both admin-group.js.es6 controller and group.js model will drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain similar offset clamping/pagination calculations in two places (admin controller `next/previous` uses `Math.min/Math.max` with `limit`, `offset`, `user_count`; model `findMembers` also clamps `offset`). However, the proposed finding claims this "will drift", which is speculative/maintainability-focused and not a verifiable defect or correctness bug introduced by the diff. Both pieces of logic are currently consistent and work together (controller sets offset; model re-clamps before request).

adjudication_records.issue_text: View/pagination state (limit, offset, user_count, members) stored on the domain model Discourse.Group couples all consumers to admin UI state

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add pagination-related fields (`limit`, `offset`) and a UI-facing collection (`members`) onto `Discourse.Group`, and `findMembers()` mutates those fields. However, this is an architectural/design concern rather than a clear defect: the model is explicitly used by both admin and non-admin group member UIs in this diff (the public `group-members` route now calls `model.findMembers()` and the template iterates `members`), and `asJSON()`/`save()`/`create()` do not serialize these pagination fields back to the server. There’s no verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness break shown in the diff that results from this coupling itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unused property userCountDisplay in discourse/models/group.js is dead code

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not provide evidence that `userCountDisplay` is unused or dead. The property already exists and is only slightly reformatted (`if (c > 0) { return c; }`). Determining “unused” would require checking template/controller usage outside this diff; within the diff we only see `{{user_count}}` used, which does not prove `userCountDisplay` is dead code. This is therefore not a verifiable defect introduced or demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of resolved promise when name is empty, breaking contract for future .then() callers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Discourse.Group#findMembers` from `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` when `name` is empty to `return;` (undefined). That does change the method’s return type in that edge case. However, within this diff all call sites that previously did `.then(...)` on `findMembers()` (the `afterModel` hooks) were removed and replaced with fire-and-forget `model.findMembers();`, and the new callers (`next/previous/removeMember/addMembers`) also don’t chain `.then`. So the finding’s claim that it breaks a contract for `.then()` callers is not directly verifiable from the diff (it’s speculative about other/future callers).

adjudication_records.issue_text: group-members route setupController sets model to the group but members stored on model not controller, template each over members may render empty
add_members silently skips unknown usernames and returns success_json, giving admin UI no feedback; JS addMembers has no error handler and input never cleared

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown usernames are simply ignored with no error collection. It then returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero users were added, so the client cannot know some entries were invalid. On the client, `actions.addMembers` just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` without any `.then/.catch` handling, and it explicitly contains `// TODO: should clear the input` with no implementation, so the input is not cleared and errors are not surfaced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member calls group.users.delete (already persists) followed by meaningless group.save/error branch that is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then conditionally responds based on `group.save`. In Rails, `association.delete` removes the join record immediately (it’s not staged on the parent for a later `save`), so the subsequent `group.save` does not control whether the member removal is persisted. This makes the save/error branch logically disconnected from the operation performed; in the unlikely event `group.save` returns false (validations/callbacks), the controller could report an error even though the user was already removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin GroupsController update/create no longer accept nested group payload and PATCH changes endpoint removed, silently breaking API consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Admin::GroupsController API contract: `create` now reads top-level params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`) instead of `params[:group][:name]` / `params[:group][:visible]` / `params[:group][:usernames]`, and `update` now reads top-level params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) instead of nested `params[:group]`. It also removes the PATCH-specific incremental membership update path (`update_patch` handling `params[:changes][:add/delete]`) entirely. Existing clients sending the previous nested payload or relying on PATCH changes will no longer work (they’ll be ignored or error), which is a verifiable breaking change introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage for new add_members/remove_member endpoints beyond happy path (e.g. nonexistent username no-op, removing non-member)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reduce/alter test coverage: prior incremental add/delete behaviors (including adding nonexistent users and removing non-members) had specs, and the new `add_members` context only tests automatic-group rejection and a successful add. There’s no explicit spec for nonexistent usernames or removing non-members. However, this is not a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the code itself—it's a testing completeness concern rather than a correctness/security problem demonstrated in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination math over-counts totalPages when user_count % limit == 0, showing an empty last page

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` when `user_count != 0`. If `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50 users with limit 50), this returns 2 instead of 1. The `next` action can set `offset` to `user_count` (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), and `findMembers` will request that offset, which the server honors (`offset(params[:offset].to_i)`), producing an empty members list. `currentPage` becomes 2 (`floor(50/50)+1`) and `showingLast` becomes true, meaning the UI can show an empty last page. This matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: next() clamps offset with Math.min(offset + limit, user_count), producing a phantom page showing zero members while claiming a valid page

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `next()` sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, which allows `offset` to become exactly `user_count`. In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, that `offset` is passed through to `/groups/:name/members.json`, and the server does `limit(limit).offset(offset)`; when `offset == total`, the result set is empty. The UI will still show a seemingly valid page because `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50 => 3 pages). That combination yields a “phantom” last page with zero members (e.g., page 3/3) after navigating next from page 2.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when group name is empty, breaking .then() chaining for callers
Public members endpoint has no cap on limit/offset params, allowing DoS via limit=100000000 and unvalidated offset (negatives/huge values)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then directly applies them via `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound or validation. This means a request like `?limit=100000000` can force the DB/app to attempt to return an extremely large member set, and a negative offset (e.g. `?offset=-5`) will be passed through (which can error at the SQL level on many DBs). The diff does not introduce any capping/clamping on the server side, so the finding is verifiable from the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops invalid usernames yet still returns success_json

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; non-existent/invalid usernames are simply skipped. After the loop it calls `group.save` and, if it succeeds (which it typically will even if no users were added), it returns `render json: success_json` with no indication that some/all usernames were invalid. This matches the finding: invalid usernames are dropped silently while still returning success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members loop is not transactional, so mid-loop failure leaves partial membership with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are iterated and `group.add(user)` is called per user without an explicit DB transaction. However, the finding’s key claim—“mid-loop failure leaves partial membership with no error surfaced”—is not directly verifiable from the diff: there is no shown failure mode for `group.add` (it may raise, it may be idempotent, it may validate), and errors would not necessarily be “not surfaced” (an exception would typically bubble to a 500). The diff does show silent skipping of unknown usernames (`if user = ...`), but that appears intentional rather than an error. So the criticism is largely speculative beyond what the diff proves.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec for remove_member that asserted silent invalid behavior was deleted, removing the safety net

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a previously-existing `remove_member` spec being deleted. In fact, a new `context ".remove_member"` is being introduced at the end of the spec file (though the diff is truncated). The tests that were deleted are for the old PATCH-based incremental membership updates (e.g., "succeeds silently when removing non-members"), not for `remove_member`. Therefore the finding misreads the diff and is not a verifiable problem introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member never reports failure when user is not a member or doesn't exist — silent success on no-op delete

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. ActiveRecord association `delete` is intentionally a no-op when the target row/user or membership doesn’t exist (it just deletes 0 join rows), so “silent success on no-op delete” is expected/idempotent DELETE behavior, not a verifiable defect. The diff also shows prior membership-removal behavior was tolerant of missing users/non-members (e.g., old incremental update/delete path did not error on non-existent users), so this isn’t clearly an introduced bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec/route verb mismatch: remove_member specs use xhr :put but route defines delete, causing specs to fail and leaving the guard untested

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin group member removal endpoint is declared as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, while in the modified controller spec a `.remove_member` example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` (visible at the end of the diff). That is a real verb mismatch: a real HTTP PUT to `/admin/groups/:group_id/members` would route to `add_members` (the PUT route), not `remove_member`, so the spec is not exercising the route that production uses and would not catch routing/verb errors for the guard. The claim that it will necessarily make the controller spec fail is less certain because controller specs can bypass routing, but the mismatch itself is verifiable and problematic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group-members template binds members but controller model is now the Group; if controller is an ArrayController, members list renders empty silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `group/members.hbs` to iterate `{{#each m in members}}` instead of `model`, and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now sets `members` on the *group model* via `self.setProperties({ ..., members: ... })`. The `group-members` route now sets `controller.set("model", model)` where `model` is the Group, then calls `model.findMembers()`, which populates `model.members`. In Ember templates, property lookup will proxy through the controller to its model, so `members` can resolve to `model.members` and update when `findMembers()` completes. The proposed finding hinges on the controller being an `ArrayController` and therefore rendering empty “silently”, but the controller type is not shown in the diff, and the template no longer depends on the controller’s `model` being an array. So this is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale user_count is used to clamp offset in findMembers before the AJAX call, causing pagination to land past the end or show stale count
After group.create(), findMembers() is never called so members area and user_count show wrong values until manual refresh

adjudication.rationale: In the updated admin group UI, the members section is only rendered when `id` is present (`{{#if id}} ... {{each member in members}} ...`). For a newly created group, there are no members to load (the create flow no longer accepts usernames; membership is added later via the explicit `addMembers` action which does call `findMembers()` afterward). While it’s true that `save`/`create` actions do not explicitly call `findMembers()`, this does not make `user_count` or the members area “wrong”: `user_count` is initialized to 0 on the model and an empty member list is the correct state immediately after creation. The diff does not show any automatic member seeding on create that would require an immediate refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames input is not cleared after addMembers, so repeated clicks re-add the same users

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action contains a comment `// TODO: should clear the input` and then calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without ever resetting `usernames` (e.g., to `null`/`""`). This means the usernames field remains populated after adding, so clicking the "Add" button again will submit the same usernames again (at minimum causing redundant requests; whether the server actually creates duplicates depends on backend constraints not shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames now lives as an ad-hoc property on the group model instead of a controller computed property, polluting the model via user-selector binding

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not move `usernames` onto the `Discourse.Group` model. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `usernames` is now a plain controller property (`usernames: null`), and the template binds `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}` to that controller property. The group model’s `asJSON()` no longer includes `usernames`, and there is no `this.set('usernames', ...)` on the model. The model does gain an ad-hoc `members` property via `findMembers()` (`self.setProperties({ ..., members: ... })`), but that is distinct from `usernames` and is not what the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: get "users" admin route removed with no verification that no frontend code still hits /admin/groups/:id/users

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the admin groups sub-route `get "users"` and introduces `put "members"` and `delete "members"` instead. In the same diff, the frontend JS is updated to call `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` for add/remove operations (see `Discourse.Group#addMembers` and `#removeMember`) and group member fetching is moved to `/groups/:name/members.json`. There is no remaining reference in the diff to `/admin/groups/:id/users`, so the claim that frontend code still hits that endpoint is not verifiable from this change set and is speculative.
